A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Quantum latent distributions in deep generative models. The text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data and QM9 experiments, including simulated and real photonic processors, plus CIFAR-10 and flow-matching results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including numerical benchmarks, generated examples and negative results.

M1.justification: Section IV.B changes the QM9 generator description from non-decreasing layers except the final layer to all layers being non-decreasing. Appendix E also changes five hidden layers to five layers while retaining identical widths and components. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents an architectural modification or a wording correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture, synthetic quantum, Bernoulli, QM9, CIFAR-10 and moons datasets and tasks. Diffusion and flow-matching demonstrations are retained in the appendices rather than removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including appendix comparisons. Quantum and Photonic rename Boson sampler and Distinguishable sampler in the main benchmarks; Gaussian and Bernoulli retain their respective participation.

E3.justification: Appendix H corrects the negative QM9 experiment's stated latent dimension from 16 to 32, agreeing with Table VIII in both versions. This is a reported-setting correction, not evidence of rerunning the experiment; its learning rate, augmentation probability and training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The latent-size and circuit comparisons, real-device checks, training curves, extended-training Gaussian-mixture analysis and Appendix H negative experiments are retained. Revised explanations of these findings do not introduce additional ablations or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts and standard-error practices remain unchanged: 12 runs for the synthetic benchmarks, 20 seeds for QM9 and five seeds for CIFAR-10 experiments. Appendix H adds a nonsignificance assertion but documents no new statistical test or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables I–VIII and the retained empirical plots and examples are unchanged. Appendix H revises its qualitative findings: instead of saying results are worse overall, v2 acknowledges improved Gaussian performance under the altered training settings and asserts no statistically significant differences between latents. Both PDFs already report Gaussian FCD 1.554 in Table VIII versus 1.823 in Table II under different settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises Corollary 1's proof to explicitly select generators from the assumed GAN-distance bound before deriving the contradiction, and corrects the approximating distribution in the quantum-sampling definition. Appendix B corrects the permanent's product index from i=i to i=1. The principal theorem and corollary statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 refocuses its advertised contributions on theory, mechanism intuition and controlled GAN benchmarking. Diffusion/flow compatibility leaves the abstract and contribution list but remains demonstrated in the appendices. The central conditional expressivity and empirical-advantage claims persist.

C2.justification: Section III.D retains the inductive-bias and non-factorizability hypotheses but expands their explanation through correlated representations and comparisons with classically transformable distributions. It explicitly acknowledges that non-uniformity and correlations are not uniquely quantum. The QM9 model's correspondence to the theorem is stated more strongly, and the discussion of classical alternatives and negative results is revised.

D1.justification: Technical documentation receives limited revisions: Appendix H corrects the latent dimension to match Table VIII, and Appendix E removes hidden from its layer description. Listed widths, implementation links, optimizers, hardware, sampling resources and training-time disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on flow-matching source distributions, generator inversion, determinantal diversity methods and a newer classical boson-sampling emulator. It removes VAE references and the appendix's state-of-the-art survey. These update supporting context while retaining the central positioning around theoretical foundations and controlled latent-distribution comparisons.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, mechanism discussion and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The former diffusion/flow-matching section is incorporated into Appendices F–G, the discussion is reorganized around classical alternatives, and sampler terminology changes throughout much of the main text. This substantially changes the narrative despite stable empirical content.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the separate Gaussian-mixture plot and experimental schematic with an integrated introductory overview, redraws the complexity and delay-loop diagrams, and relocates the flow-matching figure to the appendices. Tables are relabeled and reflowed; Table III also drops the 1-3-9 identifier from one Quantum row. Existing empirical graphics are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The more explicit corollary argument, corrected account of Table VIII and clearer organization support a modest overall improvement, while preserving the empirical evidence and negative examples. The gains are limited by unresolved stronger wording about the QM9 architecture and an added nonsignificance assertion without a specified test.
